title: DNS Server Go
tagline: Recursive DNS resolver with UDP/TCP handling and TTL caching implemented in Go.
bullets: Implemented UDP listener on port 1053 to accept DNS queries and dispatch goroutine-based handlers per request.
Parsed DNS headers, questions, answers, authority, and additional sections with domain name compression support.
Constructed DNS response headers and serialized packets with strict count validation to avoid malformed responses.
Resolved queries recursively from root name servers, following NS referrals and CNAME chains with a depth limit of 10.
Preferred IPv4 upstream addresses when selecting nameservers and fell back to IPv6 when none were available.
Retried truncated UDP responses over TCP to obtain complete answers when the TC flag is set.
Cached responses by domain and record type using minimum TTL or SOA minimum TTL values and scheduled periodic cleanup.
Propagated EDNS0 OPT additional records from client queries into responses while honoring recursion desired and available flags.
Supported encoding of A, AAAA, NS, MX, CNAME, TXT, SOA, PTR, and OPT records through dedicated serializers.
architecture: The entrypoint binds UDP port 1053, reading queries into goroutine handlers that parse packets and construct responses via the dns package. A recursive resolver contacts upstream name servers starting from the root set, prefers IPv4, follows NS referrals and CNAME chains up to a depth limit, and falls back to TCP when UDP responses are truncated. A TTL-aware cache stores answers keyed by domain and type, with periodic cleanup, while EDNS0 OPT additional records are preserved in responses.
